title: record:quick_actions still shows its refused-array developer placeholder ("refused at index N (see console)") to customers at runtime
body:
Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`) from the objectui#12995 dev report on PR #12999 (out-of-scope finding 1). The contract review of that PR judged it worth its own card. ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and routing are triage's.

## What
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-quick-actions.tsx:330` (objectui `origin/main`) draws `record:quick_actions — KEY refused at index N (see console)` in a dashed box when the block's declared action array is refused by the objectui#7182 rule (a malformed entry).
- It draws this at runtime too, so a customer on a published page that an author shipped malformed sees developer copy pointing at a console they cannot read.
- objectui#12995 (PR #12999) made the other two empty cases quiet at runtime: a block whose named actions are all withheld draws nothing, and a block naming no action shows its placeholder only under `PreviewModeProvider`. That card's ruling left the refused path unchanged.

## Question for the ruling
Whether a runtime refusal is shown, hidden (placeholder on a preview surface only, as for "named none"), or logged to the console only. The console message at `:96` already exists in every case.

## Done when
The refused array's surface text follows the ruling at runtime, and the objectui#7182 pins (`record-quick-actions.declared-action-ids-7182.test.tsx`) still separate "refused" from "empty".

## Dedupe
Searched for: `refused at index`, `quick_actions refused placeholder runtime`, `record block developer copy runtime`.
